paper_title: Knowing You Don't Know Learning When to Continue Search in Multi-round   RAG through Self-Practicing
caption: Ablation study on different Critic model choices. Both follow the SIM-RAG setting with GPT-4 as the Reasoner, but the blue bar uses learned Flan-T5-783M as a Critic, while the red bar uses GPT-4 as the Critic (a.k.a., self-critique).
model_annotation: The bar chart presents an ablation study comparing the performance of two different Critic models—Flan-T5-783M (represented by blue bars) and GPT-4 (represented by red bars)—within the SIM-RAG framework, where GPT-4 is used as the Reasoner. The horizontal axis displays six evaluation tasks: TriviaQA (EM), HotPotQA (EM), 2Wiki (EM), TriviaQA (F1), HotPotQA (F1), and 2Wiki (F1), with each task having two bars corresponding to the two Critic models. The vertical axis represents the performance score, ranging from 25 to 85, with major gridlines at intervals of 10. For all tasks, the blue bar (Flan-T5-783M) consistently achieves a higher score than the red bar (GPT-4). Specifically, in TriviaQA (EM), the scores are 77.3 (Flan-T5-783M) and 77.1 (GPT-4); in HotPotQA (EM), 37.0 and 31.9; in 2Wiki (EM), 44.5 and 32.5; in TriviaQA (F1), 82.8 and 83.8; in HotPotQA (F1), 49.7 and 43.3; and in 2Wiki (F1), 53.3 and 38.1. The chart indicates that Flan-T5-783M performs better than GPT-4 in most metrics except for TriviaQA (F1), where GPT-4 slightly outperforms it.
